summary: This is the GitHub README page for the humble branch of the gazebosim/ros_gz repository, which provides integration between ROS (1 and 2) and Gazebo simulation. It lists the repository's packages (ros_gz metapackage, ros_gz_image, ros_gz_bridge, ros_gz_sim, ros_gz_sim_demos, ros_gz_point_cloud), a compatibility table of ROS 2 and Gazebo versions, and instructions for installing binaries or building from source for ROS Humble. Page navigation and site boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: README for the ros_gz humble branch, covering ROS Humble and Gazebo integration packages, version compatibility, and install steps.
key_facts: The ros_gz repository, maintained under the gazebosim organization, is described as integration between ROS (1 and 2) and Gazebo simulation.
The humble branch supports ROS Humble.
Humble binaries are available for Fortress and are hosted at https://packages.ros.org.
Binary install uses the command: sudo apt install ros-humble-ros-gz.
The ros_gz_bridge package is a bidirectional transport bridge between Gazebo Transport and ROS.
The ros_gz_image package is a unidirectional transport bridge for images from Gazebo Transport to ROS using image_transport.
The ros_gz_sim package provides convenient launch files and executables for using Gazebo Sim with ROS.
The ros_gz_point_cloud package provides plugins for publishing point clouds to ROS from Gazebo Sim simulations.
The compatibility table lists Humble paired with Fortress, Garden and Harmonic Gazebo versions.
The ros_ign prefixed packages are shim packages that redirect to their ros_gz counterpart.
To build from source, the GZ_VERSION environment variable is set to the Gazebo version to compile against, such as edifice.
The README warns that ros_gz makes heavy use of templates, which can make compilers consume a lot of memory; building with colcon build --parallel-workers=1 --executor sequential is suggested.
The repository is Apache-2.0 licensed and had 184 stars, 118 forks and 36 open issues at the time of capture.
The repository was tagged as a ROS 2 integration repository with topics including ros2, robotics-simulation and gazebo, and was presented as having a ROSCon 2022 video.
